Have you ever been listening to a song and your body has a reaction? Maybe it’s goosebumps, or even shedding a few tears. Unexplainable host Noam Hassenfeld and Sylvan Esso’s Amelia Meath both had the same question: Why does music create these bodily responses? Noam talked to Elizabeth Margulis,  director of the Music Cognition Lab at Princeton University, to get answers. 

Listen to the episode on Netflix, or wherever you get your podcasts.

Presented by @sonos.

snippet.description:
Is there a humane way for the state to kill someone?

Subscribe to our channel! http://goo.gl/0bsAjO

Guest host Miles Bryan sits down with New York Times Magazine writer and ProPublica reporter Pamela Colloff to pull back the curtain on critical flaws in America's approach to the death penalty. From the tragedy of wrongful convictions to the profound impact capital punishment  has on victims' families, can the death penalty ever truly be justified?

Drawing on decades of reporting and a new book, To Catch a Devil, Colloff examines the reality of executions in states like Florida, the prevalence of unreliable jailhouse informants, and why a system built on human judgment can never be infallible.

06:57 The declining use of the death penalty

snippet.description:
Preparing for UPSC CSE with an optional subject? Karandeep Singh Sir, Anthropology faculty at LevelUp IAS, explains how to build the right routine for UPSC Optional preparation and answer writing.
After every class, dedicate one hour to revising the topics discussed and one hour to writing two answers. In the beginning, focus on building content and reproducing it effectively on paper rather than rushing to finish within a time limit. Speed and time management improve with regular practice.

Watch this short to understand how to prepare your optional subject systematically for UPSC Mains.

#UPSC #UPSCPreparation #UPSCOptional #AnthropologyOptional #UPSCMains #AnswerWriting #KarandeepSingh #LevelUpIAS #UPSCStrategy #CivilServicesExam
